title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are delighted to be working with a successful and growing business that is looking to appoint an experienced Accounts Assistant.

This is a varied, hands-on role covering the full range of transactional finance. It would suit someone with a strong grounding in accounts who also has some payroll experience and enjoys taking ownership of their work.

Working as part of a small collaborative finance team, your responsibilities will include:
- Managing the purchase ledger, including processing invoices and supplier payments
- Raising sales invoices and maintaining the sales ledger
- Completing bank and credit card reconciliations
- Processing employee expenses
- Resolving supplier and customer account queries
- Supporting credit control and monitoring outstanding balances
- Assisting with payroll preparation and processing
- Maintaining accurate employee and payroll records
- Supporting month-end processes, including reconciliations and journal preparation
- Ensuring finance records are complete, accurate and kept up to date
- Providing wider support to the finance team as required

The successful candidate will:
- Have previous experience in a broad transactional finance role
- Have some practical payroll experience
- Be comfortable managing both purchase and sales ledger activities
- Demonstrate excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Be organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicate confidently with colleagues, customers and suppliers
- Have good Excel skills and experience using accounting software

If you are an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity, we would love to hear from you

title: Billing & Finance Assistant
description:
Join a growing organisation and support high-volume AP, AR, billing, reconciliations and payment processing within a fast-paced finance team. This is a hybrid Leeds-based opportunity on a initial 6-month FTC with strong permanent potential, and the chance to play a key role in the company's ongoing finance transformation journey.

Client Details

This professional services organisation is based in Leeds.

Description

You'll play a key role in supporting the day-to-day finance operation, with responsibilities including:
- Processing incoming and outgoing payments
- Cash allocation and account reconciliations
- Billing and invoicing activities
- Producing and issuing statements
- Performing bank reconciliations
- Supporting month-end close processes
- Maintaining accurate financial records
- Building strong working relationships with internal stakeholders and fee earners
- Supporting a busy finance function with a variety of transactional finance duties

Profile

We're keen to speak with candidates who can demonstrate:
- Experience within transactional finance, legal cashiering, accounts payable, accounts receivable or billing
- Strong reconciliation skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Confident communication skills and the ability to work with stakeholders at all levels
- A proactive and inquisitive approach
- Resilience and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment

Job Offer

- 35-hour working week
- Flexible start and finish times
- Leeds city centre location
- Immediate start available
- Initial 6-month fixed-term contract
- Strong potential to secure a permanent position

This role would suit someone who enjoys getting involved, asking questions, improving processes and making a genuine impact within a finance team undergoing positive change.

title: Bookkeeper / Accounts Assistant
company: BC Financial Search Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
BC Financial Search is working with an established accountancy practice in Leeds to recruit an experienced Bookkeeper / Accounts Assistant to join their team on a full-time basis.

This is a broad, hands-on position suited to somebody with good experience working within an accountancy practice or bookkeeping environment who enjoys managing their own workload and having regular contact with clients.

The role will be predominantly office-based in Leeds, with occasional travel to client premises where required.

The firm is open-minded on qualification level. You could be studying towards AAT, already AAT qualified, or simply have strong practical experience and be qualified by experience. Study support can also be provided for somebody who would like to continue their professional development.

Salary is expected to be in the region of £32,000-£40,000, depending on experience.

Duties and responsibilities

The successful candidate will work across a varied portfolio of clients, with responsibilities including:
- Completing bookkeeping for a range of businesses and sole traders
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Supporting clients with Making Tax Digital requirements and submissions
- Preparing management accounts
- Maintaining accurate accounting records and reconciliations
- Working extensively with cloud accounting software including Xero and QuickBooks
- Liaising directly with clients regarding their bookkeeping and accounting requirements
- Visiting client premises when required
- Supporting the wider accounts team with additional accounting work where appropriate

The position offers plenty of variety and would suit somebody who enjoys working directly with clients rather than performing a purely transactional bookkeeping role.

Experience and qualifications

The firm is flexible regarding formal qualifications and is particularly interested in candidates with strong practical bookkeeping experience.

Ideally, you will have:
- Previous bookkeeping experience, ideally gained within an accountancy practice or similar environment
- Good working knowledge of Xero and QuickBooks
- Experience preparing VAT returns
- Knowledge of Making Tax Digital requirements
- Some exposure to management accounts
- Good attention to detail and organisational skills
- Confidence communicating directly with clients
- The ability to manage your own workload and deadlines

Candidates may be:
- Studying towards an AAT qualification
- Already AAT qualified
- Qualified by experience with a strong bookkeeping background

Benefits

The role offers:
- Salary of £32,000-£40,000, depending on experience
- Full-time permanent position
- Study support available for candidates looking to continue their qualifications
- Broad bookkeeping and accounting responsibilities
- Regular client contact
- Exposure to a varied portfolio of businesses
- Opportunity to develop beyond traditional bookkeeping into areas such as management accounts

Company culture

The firm is a well-established Leeds accountancy practice providing a broad range of accounting, tax and advisory services to its clients.

This role would suit somebody who values being part of an office-based team and enjoys building strong relationships with both colleagues and clients.

The position provides a good balance between day-to-day bookkeeping responsibilities and broader accounting work, with the opportunity to continue developing technically and professionally.

For more information or a confidential discussion about the position, please apply or contact BC Financial Search directly.

title: Casualty Claims Handler

A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims, predominantly EL & PL and Third-Party Property Damage losses.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.

- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

title: Claims Handler (Top Insurance Company)
description:
It should be no surprise that when this dynamic insurer decided to build a London Market Claims Team in the UK regions, it plumped for Leeds - it has been established locally for over 20 years, already boasts a significant claims team that comprises many of the region's most gifted insurance professionals, and has recently invested significantly in the acquisition of penthouse offices in perhaps Leeds' most prestigious office addresses.

It is arguably the most exciting insurance company in the market right now, using ingenuity combined with technical expertise and cutting-edge technology to underwrite risks that other insurers shy away from. This 'can do' attitude, coupled with an unwavering focus on client service, is serving it well; the business is currently enjoying 20% year on year growth, and is well on track to exceed its plans to double in size within 5 years.

Working in this new team, you will be handling specialist Professional Indemnity claims from a range of industry sectors such as Solicitors, Architects, Engineers and Consultants. You'll take responsibility for handling a portfolio of high-volume claims from first notification of loss through to final settlement. You'll update in-house and London market claim related systems in relation to individual claims and ensure stakeholders are kept apprised of key developments and key information. In addition, you'll diarise and triage claims as required by the Claims Handling Manual and subject these decisions to regular challenge and review. You'll also develop and maintain excellent working relationships with brokers, as well as working with the Claims Manager on claims initiatives and projects to reach specific goals.

You DO NOT need to have experience in Professional Indemnity claims as full training will be provided. However, you must have some previous experience in insurance claims handling. We are open to experience here and will consider claims specialists from a range of backgrounds, including but not limited to, personal lines, commercial or healthcare insurance. Crucially, you must be well-organised and efficient, with strong communication skills and the ability to analyse claims data in order to spot trends. Just as importantly, you'll have good IT (Microsoft Office) skills, including Word, Excel and Outlook, together with the ability to quickly learn new in-house systems.

Our client is based a stone's throw from Leeds railway station, close to the main public transport links and all the amenities the city centre has to offer. You will be welcome to work from home 1 day per week. In addition to a generous basic salary, you will receive a fantastic benefits package that includes a lucrative bonus and an impressive pension arrangement.

title: Client Money Controls Coordinator
company: Everywhen, part of the Ardonagh Group - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are looking for a highly organised and analytical Client Money Controls Coordinator to join our Finance and IBA Operations team. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in maintaining and enhancing our Client & Insurer Money control framework while supporting a strong regulatory environment across the business.

Working closely with stakeholders across Operations, Risk & Compliance, Finance and Client Money Audit, you will help ensure our controls remain robust, effective and compliant with FCA Client Asset Sourcebook (CASS) requirements. You will also be responsible for coordinating control attestations, supporting regulatory reporting and driving continuous improvements across the client money control environment.

This role would suit someone with experience in financial services, risk, controls, audit, compliance or client money operations who is looking to further develop their expertise within a regulatory and governance-focused environment.

What will you do as a Client Money Controls Coordinator?
- Oversee and proactively review Client & Insurer Money controls through our risk management framework and online risk event portal.
- Coordinate quarterly control attestation processes with key stakeholders across the business.
- Support the implementation of new controls and enhancements to existing control processes.
- Maintain the CASS Risk Assessment, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, documented and linked to effective controls.
- Produce monthly client money reporting, management information and analytics.
- Maintain the central breach register, ensuring all CASS 5 and CASS 8 breaches are accurately recorded and monitored.
- Build strong working relationships with senior stakeholders, operational teams and external auditors.
- Identify control gaps, process inefficiencies and opportunities for continuous improvement.
- Support compliance with FCA Client Asset Sourcebook requirements and internal governance standards.

What are we looking for in our next Client Money Controls Coordinator?
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills with a high level of attention to detail.
- Analytical and investigative problem-solving abilities.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
- Confidence working independently and collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.
- Knowledge of CASS regulations, particularly CASS 5 and CASS 8.
- Experience working within a regulated financial services environment.
- Previous experience within the insurance sector.
- Exposure to risk, controls, audit, compliance or client money functions.

In return you will be welcomed and supported by our Ardonagh family joining an organisation that cares about you as a person and your wellbeing. Some of the other benefits are:
- Holiday entitlement of 26 days plus bank holidays, increasing with length of service
- 35 hour working week
- Opportunity to progress your career across the entire Ardonagh family
- Award-winning learning & development offering and support to obtain professional qualifications to enhance your knowledge and career prospects
- Pension scheme for when you feel it's time to retire
- 24-hour Employee Assistance support for you and your family's physical and mental wellbeing
- Corporate perks such as discounted gym memberships, cinema tickets, shopping, Eyecare vouchers, cycle to work and much more
- One day paid volunteering to give back to our communities
- Ardonagh Community Trust (ACT) - raising funds for charity with donation matching in your local community
- The Spotlight Awards, where we celebrate the best of the Ardonagh Group and all the bright talent across our business.

We offer genuine potential for both personal and professional development, come and be part of our story and help us shape our future. So, what are you waiting for? Apply today and one of our team will be in touch.

INDX3

Everywhen is an equal opportunities employer, with a growing and thriving diversity, equity and inclusion strategy; we are committed to a working environment that is free from discrimination, is inclusive, and empowers our people to bring their whole self to work and reach their full potential.

If your application is successful, we will conduct relevant employment checks prior to you commencing employment with us. These will include verifying your recent employment, address, credit history and a standard criminal record check.

As an Everywhen colleague, you will be expected to uphold our values, act professionally and respectfully towards others, and contribute to a workplace where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. We expect all colleagues to help maintain an environment free from bullying, harassment, victimisation and other inappropriate behaviours, supporting our commitment to an inclusive and high-performing culture.

title: Distribution Coordinator
description:
About Breedon Group:
Breedon Group plc is a leading vertically integrated construction materials group in Great Britain, Ireland, and the USA. We're dedicated to providing high-quality materials and services for the construction industry, with a commitment to safety, sustainability, and innovation. Joining Breedon means becoming part of a team that values excellence and is committed to making a positive impact.

Position Overview:
The primary responsibiltity of the Distribution Coordinator is to provide customers with the highest standards of customer service ensuring that we effectively plan and meet customer promises by delivering in full and on time, whilst optimising EBIT.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain visibility of production and transport availability to enable proactive influencing of distribution plan development
- Capture and place customer orders in line with quotations ensuring that information is accurately captured within Breedon's systems and in adherence with defined processes
- Build and optimise a distribution plan which enables product delivery to meet customer needs and which supports development of a balanced and efficient distribution plan, liaising with the Commercial Team, Operations Team and Transport Team where needed to enable this
- Plan driver rest times and proactively manage and enable adherence to H&S policy
- Contact all customers on the day prior to delivery to confirm orders and delivery schedule
- Respond to changes in the plan driven by customer circumstance, production availability etc, minimising customer impact where possible, proactively contacting customers to alert them to changes which will impact delivery
- Ensure transport and distribution process compliance and maintain data integrity to enable informed decision making, including the capture of declined orders and lost volume
- Build and maintain strong relationships with customers, over the phone, to understand potential sales opportunities and alert the Commercial Team where appropriate
- Proactively influence and review shared performance KPIs (eg. Plan adherence) to drive improvement in customer experience and distribution efficiency
- Implement changes to ways of working in line with Customer & Commercial Excellence initiatives.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

You'll enjoy;
- managing competing priorities and a dynamic work environment
- overcoming operations and logistics challenges to delight customers
- maintaining focus on outcomes in a constantly changing environment

You'll be;
- a highly effective communicator and facilitator, able to collaborate across teams and levels
- a self-starter who is commercially focused and responds appropriately on your own to improve outcomes and process's and assumes responsibility for your own performance
- proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel and Powerpoint) Word and experience with CRM software

You'll have strong;
- organisational and multitasking skills
- analytical skills with the ability to generate insights from data
- verbal and written communication
- attention to detail and a right first time attitude
- effective conflict resolution and is adaptable and resilient.

Benefits
- A tailored, competitive salary
- Company Pension Scheme
- 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays on top (Scotland - 33 days annual leave, inclusive of bank holidays)
- Share Saver Scheme participation
- Company Life Assurance Scheme
- Access to our Employee Assistance Programme for health and wellbeing support
- Discounts on a wide range of products through our employee benefits platform
- Broad learning opportunities and career progression pathways.

Diversity Statement:
At Breedon Group, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity is valued. We believe in equality of opportunity for all and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates.

Join Us:
If you're looking for a role that challenges you, offers progression, and contributes to building better futures, we'd love to hear from you. This position is an opportunity to grow your career within a supportive and dynamic environment at Breedon Group.

Application Process:
Ready to make a meaningful difference? Apply now by submitting your CV and cover letter. We look forward to considering your application and potentially welcoming you to our team.

title: HR Onboarding Coordinator
description:
The Opportunity

This is a fantastic opportunity to join our client, a global insurance firm, in their Leeds office as an HR Onboarding Coordinator on a 12-month fixed-term contract.

Working closely with HR, Talent Acquisition and hiring managers, you will take ownership of the onboarding process from offer acceptance through to a new starter's first day. You will coordinate pre-employment screening, background checks, contracts, references and new joiner communications, ensuring candidates and managers are kept informed throughout.

This is a highly organised, people-focused role where you will be responsible for keeping the process moving, proactively chasing outstanding actions and providing a seamless candidate experience.

Key Accountabilities
- Coordinate pre-employment screening, right to work and compliance checks, escalating any issues where required.
- Support with reference checking and develop an understanding of DBS requirements and the legal requirements behind screening decisions.
- Prepare and issue contracts, ensuring any adjustments are captured correctly and escalated for approval. Contracts should be issued within 48 hours of initial notification.
- Act as a key point of contact for candidates, responding to queries and providing regular updates. You should be comfortable picking up the phone and speaking directly with candidates.
- Work closely with HR, Talent Acquisition and hiring managers, proactively providing updates and chasing outstanding actions.
- Ensure managers are prepared for new starters and that day-one arrangements are in place.
- Complete onboarding administration, including new joiner communications, adding candidates to relevant systems and maintaining accurate trackers.
- Monitor candidates throughout the onboarding process, including those with longer notice periods, and ensure actions remain on track.
- Audit candidate files to ensure data is accurate and up to date.
- Troubleshoot issues, identify when escalation is required and coordinate appropriate resolutions.
- Identify opportunities to improve the onboarding process and candidate experience.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who is highly organised, proactive and confident working in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

You will ideally have:
- Experience in HR, Talent Acquisition, recruitment coordination or a similar high-volume administrative role.
- Excellent communication skills and confidence speaking with candidates and stakeholders over the phone.
- Strong attention to detail, time management and problem-solving skills.
- A proactive approach to chasing outstanding information and keeping processes moving.
- The ability to manage multiple candidates, deadlines and competing priorities.
- A strong customer and candidate focus, with the ability to build relationships quickly.
- Experience using Excel and Microsoft Office.
- Workday experience would be desirable.
- Experience working with a third-party background screening provider would be advantageous.

Previous experience of pre-employment screening, DBS or compliance checks is beneficial but not essential, as training will be provided.

Why Join Us?

This is a great opportunity to build your career within HR, gaining broad experience across onboarding, pre-employment screening, compliance and candidate experience within a global insurance business.

You'll receive support during your first few months to learn the screening systems, compliance requirements and wider business, before becoming self-sufficient and taking full ownership of your workload.

If you're organised, proactive, people-focused and enjoy making sure things get done, we'd love to hear from you!

CRA Consulting are working with a leading UK legal and insurance business looking to recruit an experienced RTA Claims Handler or Paralegal into its specialist Mobility Claims team in Leeds.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience handling Road Traffic Accident personal injury claims who enjoys combining technical claims work with delivering a high standard of customer service.

You will manage your own RTA caseload, including claims progressing through the Official Injury Claim (OIC) and Ministry of Justice (MOJ) portals. Depending on experience, this could include both litigated and non-litigated matters.

The Role

Joining an established Claims team within the wider Legal Services department, you will help customers progress their RTA claims efficiently and achieve fair outcomes.

Responsibilities include:
- Managing your own RTA personal injury caseload
- Handling OIC, MOJ and non-portal claims
- Managing litigated and non-litigated matters depending on experience
- Progressing claims from instruction to settlement
- Reviewing liability, medical evidence, quantum and settlement proposals
- Obtaining evidence required to progress claims
- Liaising with customers, insurers and legal representatives
- Explaining legal and technical information clearly to customers
- Maintaining accurate case management records
- Working towards agreed quality, service and performance standards

Ideally, you will have:
- Previous RTA personal injury claims experience
- Knowledge of the OIC and/or MOJ portal
- Experience managing your own caseload
- Understanding of liability, quantum and medical evidence
- Strong communication and client-care skills
- Good organisation and file-management abilities
- Ability to manage competing deadlines
- Experience working towards quality or performance targets

Litigation experience would be advantageous but isn't essential for every appointment.

The package is particularly strong and includes:

Most employees are expected to spend at least 50% of their working time in the office each week, with flexibility around hours, part-time arrangements and job shares open to discussion.

The Business

Our client is a major UK legal and insurance business with an established customer base and strong reputation.

The organisation continues to invest in its people, technology and customer service and, due to increasing work volumes, is expanding its Leeds claims operation.

For somebody looking for stability, excellent benefits and the opportunity to develop their RTA claims career within a recognised national organisation, this is well worth exploring.

Yorkshire Design Group is an established, family-owned property business with over 35 years' experience in the development, regeneration and management of commercial property in Leeds.

With a varied portfolio of properties and interests across two group companies, we are looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant / Bookkeeper to take responsibility for the day-to-day accounting and financial administration of the business.

Your Role

The position covers a broad range of transactional accounts and bookkeeping responsibilities, with particular involvement in the financial administration of our managed properties.

Your responsibilities will include, but not limited to:
- Maintaining accurate day-to-day accounts across two group companies
- Raising sales invoices and processing tenant recharges
- Managing purchase ledger and supplier invoices
- Monitoring outstanding balances and chasing debtors
- Maintaining accurate tenant accounts and financial records
- Processing costs associated with landlords, utilities and service charges
- Dealing with invoices from contractors and other suppliers
- Completing bank reconciliations
- Maintaining accounting records within Sage
- Investigating and resolving day-to-day accounts queries
- Liaising with tenants, suppliers, landlords and contractors where required
- Working closely with the external accountant and providing financial information as required
- Supporting year-end accounting processes
- Assisting with other finance and accounts administration across the group

The nature of the business means there will be plenty of variety, and you will have the opportunity to develop a good understanding of both the financial and operational sides of the property portfolio.

Our ideal candidate

We are looking for someone with solid practical bookkeeping or accounts experience who is confident managing their own workload and maintaining accurate financial records.

You should have:
- Previous experience as an Accounts Assistant, Bookkeeper or in a similar finance position
- Practical experience using Sage
- AAT Level 3
- Experience of sales and purchase ledger
- Good knowledge of invoicing, reconciliations and credit control
- Strong numerical and administrative skills
- Good working knowledge of Excel
- Excellent attention to detail
- The confidence to communicate professionally with tenants, suppliers and other external contacts
- The ability to organise and prioritise your own workload

Experience within property, construction, commercial property or facilities management would be beneficial, although it is not essential.

A Flexible Part-Time Opportunity

We recognise that experienced people looking for part-time work often require some flexibility around their working pattern.

Our preference is approximately three days per week, although we are equally happy to consider spreading the hours across five shorter days, including a school-hours arrangement.

The position is office based at The Calls in Leeds city centre, working as part of a small, established team.

About Yorkshire Design Group

For more than 35 years, Yorkshire Design Group has been involved in the development and management of property in Leeds, combining property development with the ongoing management of its commercial assets.

As a family-owned business, we offer the opportunity to work within a close-knit organisation where you can take genuine responsibility for your area and build a long-term understanding of the business.

About the Role

Working as part of our Campaign Team, you will manage a varied range of marketing campaigns and events across the UK, from initial planning through to completion.

This role is based at our office in Pudsey. Applicants must live within a commutable distance or be planning to relocate before starting.

Key Responsibilities

Campaign Planning
- Review campaign briefs, client requirements, deadlines and budgets.
- Agree timelines, reporting requirements, purchase orders, billing details and practical arrangements with clients.
- Maintain accurate campaign information, including staffing rates, expenses, shift times and invoicing details.
- Create task plans, staffing instructions, location maps, equipment lists and campaign timelines.
- Support the recruitment, selection, vetting and briefing of suitable campaign staff.
- Coordinate venues, equipment, print, suppliers, travel, accommodation, logistics and couriers.
- Manage supplier costs and monitor expected campaign profitability.
- Complete venue documentation, health and safety planning, staff training and final pre-campaign checks.

Live Campaign Management
- Oversee live campaigns to ensure they are delivered safely and in line with the agreed brief.
- Monitor activity through photographs, feedback, results and location tracking.
- Quickly resolve any staffing, equipment, venue, logistical or performance issues.
- Provide clients with timely updates, photographs and daily or weekly reports.
- Gather accurate campaign results and feedback from staff, customers and venues.
- Record staff performance and share relevant feedback with the staffing team.
- Keep internal teams updated on client communications and campaign changes.
- Remain contactable during agreed busy weekend periods to support your live campaigns.

Post-Campaign Management
- Coordinate staff debriefs, equipment returns, campaign close-down and the organisation of reusable assets.
- Produce accurate final reports and confirm that all campaign requirements have been completed.
- Complete financial reconciliations and review campaign profitability.
- Evaluate performance and key learnings to improve future campaign delivery.
- Hold post-campaign discussions with clients and identify further opportunities.

Client and Account Development
- Build and maintain positive, long-term client relationships.
- Identify opportunities to grow existing accounts and re-engage lapsed clients.
- Keep client details and campaign records up to date within the company CRM.
- Support LINK's social media activity by sharing content about current and upcoming campaigns.

About You

We are looking for someone who has:
- Excellent communication skills and the confidence to work with clients, colleagues, suppliers and campaign staff.
- Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
- A proactive, practical approach to solving problems.

Previous marketing, events or campaign experience would be beneficial but is not essential, as full training will be provided.

The position may be particularly suited to graduates in Marketing, Events, PR or Communications who have gained some relevant work experience.
